slides.heading: What is a Boolean Expression?
slides.body: What is a Boolean Expression? is part of Boolean Logic and Comparisons. This short lesson gives you a practical Python idea you can understand, try, and reuse in simple programs.

slides.heading: Core Idea: What is a Boolean Expression?
slides.body: A boolean expression is a statement that evaluates to True or False. It is the foundation of decision-making in Python.

slides.heading: Real-World Analogy
slides.body: A boolean expression is like a yes-or-no question. The answer can only be yes or no, True or False.

slides.heading: Key Rule
slides.body: Boolean expressions must produce True or False. Use comparisons and logical operators carefully.

slides.heading: Try It Yourself!
slides.prompt: Print the result of checking whether 10 is greater than 2.

quiz.prompt_text: What are the only two possible boolean values in Python?
quiz.explanation: Correct! Python booleans are True and False — always with a capital first letter. They represent the result of any yes/no decision in code.

quiz.prompt_text: Arrange the following lines to check whether 10 is greater than 2 and print the result.
quiz.explanation: The comment describes the intent first, then print() evaluates 10 > 2 and displays the boolean result True.

quiz.prompt_text: Print the result of checking whether 10 is greater than 2.
quiz.correct_answer: Any valid Python code that satisfies the prompt.
quiz.explanation: print(10 > 2) outputs True because 10 is indeed greater than 2. Boolean expressions always evaluate to either True or False.
